$comment: Per-repo Felix config. Place as felix.config.json at the TARGET repo root. This example is for a Node/TS repo. Felix is repo-agnostic: the commands below teach it how to install/test/boot THIS repo. {file} is substituted with a test file path relative to the repo root.

drive.$comment: R1 (opt-in): after build+test, BOOT the app and probe it, catching failures that only surface at RUNTIME — a route that 404/500s, or a page that answers 200 but renders a blank screen. Default enabled=false, so non-web repos are untouched. Auto-detect pre-fills startCommand for vite/next apps; flip enabled=true and list your routes. The HTTP probe below is dependency-free (Node fetch); the pageLoad block is the deeper browser render.

pageLoad.$comment: Headless render check — catches the '200 but blank screen' class the HTTP probe can't. Needs Playwright in felix/ (`npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`); if it's absent this SKIPS softly and never flips a verdict. failOnPageError gates on uncaught exceptions (the usual blank-screen cause). Console errors are captured + reported but only gate when failOnConsoleError=true (they're noisy). minBodyChars is the blank-screen floor: fail if <body> renders fewer trimmed chars (set 0 to disable for canvas/image-only apps). requireSelector is an optional stronger assertion (e.g. '#root .app').

flowOpts.$comment: Budgets for the R1(B) interaction flows below. stepTimeoutMs bounds one action (waiting for a selector, a click, a nav); flowTimeoutMs bounds a whole flow so one wedged flow can't eat the CI job; settleMs is the pause after an interacting step so the DOM can react before the next assertion looks at it. failOnPageError makes an uncaught exception mid-flow a hard fail.

flows.$comment: R1(B) (opt-in): a page that LOADS is not a page that WORKS. 'the button does nothing', 'the form submits and nothing happens', 'login accepts a wrong password' pass both the HTTP probe and the headless render — and they're usually exactly what the PR claims. A flow clicks and asserts like a user; a failed flow is a HARD Tier 1 check. Verbs: goto click fill select press waitFor waitMs expectText expectNoText expectSelector expectNoSelector expectUrl. SAFETY (this file is attacker-controlled — whoever opens the PR writes it): steps are data not code (no eval/evaluate passthrough); goto takes a same-origin PATH only, never an absolute URL; valueEnv may ONLY name FELIX_FLOW_* vars so a PR can't type a real secret into a page it controls; typed values are redacted from every report ('fill #password ***'); a malformed flow is a hard FAIL, not a silent skip. Delete this array (or leave it empty) to run no flows.
flows.name: login rejects a bad password

secrets.$comment: Felix's built-in scan is a CHANGED-FILES BACKSTOP, not an authoritative repo scanner. For security-sensitive repos, set externalScan to a real scanner run as the HARD gate — Felix then demotes its own scan to advisory and defers. Use gitleaks (offline, no network) or trufflehog WITH verification OFF (never on — live verification fires network requests using attacker-controlled PR content: SSRF/egress risk on untrusted diffs). Empty = the built-in scan gates.

judge.$comment: Tier 3 cross-family LLM judge. adversarial=true uses a refute-first prompt — the judge must state the strongest reason each criterion is NOT met before deciding, which cuts over-eager 'met' verdicts. Off by default; FELIX_JUDGE_ADVERSARIAL=true is the global/Action equivalent.

gating.$comment: Make Felix authoritative. enabled=false (default) is advisory. When enabled, the verdicts in blockOn make the 'Felix verdict' check fail (gateable by marking it Required in branch protection); a PR carrying overrideLabel bypasses the block.

isolation.$comment: Phase 2 sandbox jail. mode 'none' (default) runs commands on the host with a clean env + timeout. mode 'docker' runs each Tier 1 step in a locked-down container: no network (except install), memory/CPU/pid caps, non-root, read-only root FS, all caps dropped. image defaults per detected language when omitted.
